Agrizero.Description:
Agrizero is an agricultural biotech firm focused on researching and deploying offworld farming technology. The company’s aim is to provide a network of self-sustaining, self-contained 'bio-factories' that will ultimately feed a projected 1 million humans in space.
Emerging from the late 21st century's environmental disasters, the firm has roots in China's world-saving artificial farming initiatives, and has now spread to facilities in the Asteroid Belt, where the supply of ice asteroids makes vertical farming and controlled-environment agriculture extremely promising.
While many of their facilities are still under construction, Agrizero is already one of the main suppliers of offworld groups like <link=ODA><color=#0080FFFF>ODA</color></link>, <link=Sinotai><color=#0080FFFF>Sinotai</color></link> and <link=ExMin><color=#0080FFFF>ExMin</color></link> through the ever-expanding Trader Network.
Agrizero.Title: Agrizero

Asura.Description:
Asura Biomedia was founded in the early 22nd century by Mumbai-based trillionaire Ashan Gurwaja. Nominally focused on 'biotechnology', the company has always had an ‘elastic’ notion of exactly what that entailed: everything from pharmaceuticals to pet food.
Gurwaja's background in bio-engineering firms put the company in the highest echelon of bio-science industries from the very beginning, and it grew exactly as its founder intended: rapidly and reliably, structured specifically to swallow up any smaller firms in its way.
Near mid-century, Asura's ambitions evolved to embrace entire health systems – it is now the largest provider of healthcare on Earth, integrating hospitals and primary care with medical supplies, pharmaceutical production and retail, residential care and funeral services.
By 2150, Asura's business was a simple proposition, as captured in their famous – if not infamous – advertising slogan: 'We're in you'.
Asura.Title: Asura Biomedia

AutomatedRocketPage.Description:
Rocket parts are printed on the <link=ThingStructureRocketManufactory><color=green>Rocket Manufactory</color></link>.

<link=ThingStructureFuselageTypeA1><color=green>Fuselage (Type A1)</color></link> must be built upon a <link=ThingStructureLaunchMount><color=green>Launch Mount</color></link>. A <link=ThingStructureGovernedGasEngine><color=green>Pumped Gas Engine</color></link> must be placed in an <link=ThingStructureEngineMountTypeA1><color=green>Engine Mount (Type A1)</color></link>.

Resource Umbilicals are placed on the <link=ThingStructureRocketTower><color=green>Launch Tower</color></link> and connect between <link=ThingStructureGasUmbilicalMale><color=green>Umbilical (Gas)</color></link> and <link=ThingStructureGasUmbilicalFemale><color=green>Umbilical Socket (Gas)</color></link> placed inside the rocket.

A <link=ThingStructureComputer><color=green>Počítač</color></link> with the <link=ThingMotherboardRockets><color=green>Rocket Control Motherboard</color></link> provides a user interface to control the rocket.

A Pair of datalinks are used to create a planet-side <link=ThingStructureLogicRocketUplink><color=green>Logic Uplink</color></link> and a rocket-side <link=ThingStructureLogicRocketDownlink><color=green>Logic Rocket Downlink</color></link> which must be hooked up to the <link=ThingStructureComputer><color=green>Počítač</color></link>.

An <link=ThingStructureRocketAvionics><color=green>Rocket Avionics</color></link> should be placed in the rocket to act as the main rocket controller.

On the <link=ThingMotherboardRockets><color=green>Rocket Control Motherboard</color></link> Map Screen you can set the rocket destination.

Igniting the rocket without a destination set allows you to see rocket performance and fuel usage without launching the rocket.

Expect to use 5-20Kmol of fuel per rocket trip, depending on rocket size.

A <link=ThingStructureRocketScanner><color=green>Rocket Scanner</color></link> is used to chart unknown locations and discover minable asteroids.

More complex rockets may use <link=ThingStructureRocketMiner><color=green>Rocket Miner</color></link> and <link=ThingStructureCargoStorageSmall><color=green>Cargo Storage (Small)</color></link>.

CHAC.Description:
Founded in 2085 to produce weapons for <link=Sinotai><color=#0080FFFF>Sinotai</color></link>'s space forces, the company is known for making highly reliable and affordable weapons for off-world use.
Their pragmatic approach is reflected in their focus on designs suitable for 3D printing and mass production, as well as a high reuse of components across models and weapon classes.
As a result, although CHAC guns excel in no particular category, and have certainly never been accused of greatness, they suffer no great failings, and perform sufficiently well by most known measures to have earned their designers the informal title of 'armorer to the Solar System'.
CHAC.Title: CHAC

CableNetworkPage.Description:
When placing cables with <link=ThingItemCableCoil><color=green>Kabelová cívka</color></link> you create cable networks. These contain volatile memory that can be read or written to using a  <link=ThingItemIntegratedCircuit10><color=green>Integrovaný obvod (IC10)</color></link>. This includes a variety of special logic variables such as <link=LogicTypeChannel0><color=orange>Channel0</color></link> through to <link=LogicTypeChannel7><color=orange>Channel7</color></link>. The networks also have readable memory, which contains a list of all the data devices on the network, and can be used with GET to find the <link=LogicTypeReferenceId><color=orange>ReferenceId</color></link> for that device. 
  
To find out the current quantity of devices in the stack, use the <link=LogicTypeStackSize><color=orange>StackSize</color></link> variable on the network, as the network adjusts its stack size dynamically based on devices within it. Cable Networks are volatile memory, and will change both their order, contents, and data whenever the network changes - so you may need to constantly poll and update the information.  

To access this, use extra notation on your device references such as <color=yellow>d0</color>:<color=yellow>1</color> to access network 1 off the provided device. To find out the connection number, check the stationpedia page for that device for the number under the connections section.

ConstructionPage.Description: Getting Started Typically you will use kits to initiate construction and then a variety of tools and resources to complete. Pay close attention to how many of your kit are required to construct what you have selected, as some structures require more than one of the stack to be consumed. For some kits you will have multiple options, use the Scroll Wheel to change the current option you are looking to build. Build States Some structures will have multiple build states that require different combinations to complete. Your tooltip will advise you of what combination you need to complete the structure. Sometimes you will need to have two objects, one in each hand, to complete a build state. Some tools will need to be turned on first, which can done by pressing Mouse3 while it's in your active hand. Tooltips If you look directly at a structure that is incomplete you will get information about what you need to do to complete it. If you have a tool in your hand and its not the right tool, a tooltip will appear telling you what you would need to use to deconstruct it. Pressure When building, it's important to note that pressure is measured as a differential. Most structures have a 200kPa pressure limit: if the difference between inside and outside is greater than that, you've got problems.
ConstructionPage.Title: Construction

DecayPage.Description:
Food decays over time into <link=ThingDecayedFood><color=green>Decayed Food</color></link>, unless refrigerated in a sutable atmosphere. The exact speed of decay varies individually by:

- TEMPERATURE - Refrigeration will slow decay, but many foods will be damaged by exposure to extreme low pressure, as well as extreme heat. The optimum temperature is 0 kelvin (-272 C).

- FOOD TYPE - Each <link=OrganicPage><color=#0080FFFF>food</color></link> type has its own decay properties. <link=ThingItemTomatoSoup><color=green>Rajčatová polévka</color></link> lasts a lot longer than a <link=ThingItemTomato><color=green>Rajče</color></link>, for instance.

- PRESSURE - Food decays faster when the pressure drops below 1 atmosphere (101kPa). Decay happens exponentially more quickly as the atmosphere approaches a perfect vacuum. There is no effect from higher pressures. 

- ATMOSPHERE - Different gases can slow and accelerate the decay process. The process will take account of respective gas ratios in mixed atmospheres in calculating the decay modifier. The following rates apply across all foods:

> <link=GasOxygen><color=#44AD83>Kyslík</color></link> x 1.3
> <link=GasNitrogen><color=#44AD83>Dusík</color></link> x 0.6
> <link=GasCarbonDioxide><color=#44AD83>Oxid uhličitý</color></link> x 0.8
> <link=GasMethane><color=#44AD83>Těkavé látky</color></link> x 1
> <link=GasPollutant><color=#44AD83>Znečišťující látka</color></link> x 3
> <link=GasNitrousOxide><color=#44AD83>Oxid dusičitý</color></link> x 1.5
> <link=GasWater><color=#44AD83>Voda</color></link> x 2
> Vacuum - see PRESSURE (above).

EVAPage.Description:
Your spacesuit provides you with a portable atmosphere, with adjustable pressure and air conditioning (temperature) settings, as well as an warning system that will alert you should the atmosphere inside the suit become hazardous. It functions in conjunction with a suitable helmet to function properly, as well as suitable gas canisters and filters in the suit's various slots. These will need to be changed regularly, and can also be recharged (or drained) using a <link=ThingStructureSuitStorage><color=green>Stojan na oblek</color></link>.

There are several suits, including the <link=ThingItemEvaSuit><color=green>Skafandr</color></link> and the more pressure- and temperature-resistant <link=ThingItemHardSuit><color=green>Zpevněný oblek</color></link>.

Your suit various readouts are at the bottom-right of the screen. Pressing the appropriate numeric key (2will bring up a panel showing its slots and settings. These include:

- A/C On / Off (i.e. Temperature control on/off)
- Filters On / Off
- Air On / Off
- Pressure Up / Down (with a range of 0kPA to 202kPa, or 0-2 Earth atmospheres)
- Temperature Up / Down (with a range of 0°C to 60°C)

Suits contains 6-8 slots:
- Air tank (x1) - insert a canister or smart canister containing a breathable gas mix, eg <link=GasOxygen><color=#44AD83>Kyslík</color></link> or <link=GasNitrogen><color=#44AD83>Dusík</color></link>/<link=GasOxygen><color=#44AD83>Kyslík</color></link> 35/65.
- Waste tank (x1) - collects gases removed by the filters
- Life support (x1) - holds one battery, which powers your A/C, lights, etc.
- <link=SlotGasFilter><color=orange>Plynový filtr</color></link> (x3) - requires at least one <link=ThingItemGasFilterCarbonDioxide><color=green>Filtr (oxid uhličitý)</color></link> (if human), depending on your breathable gas mix. Note that a <link=ThingItemHardSuit><color=green>Zpevněný oblek</color></link> has 4 filter slots.
- IC - <link=ThingItemHardSuit><color=green>Zpevněný oblek</color></link> only.

Pressure: should be set to 50-100 KPa (0.5 to 1 Earth atmospheres). Humans in-game tolerate up to ~250kPa and can survive up to ~300kPA.

Temperature: normally set to 18-21°C, with humans in-game preferring 10-29°C, tolerating 0-39°C and surviving around up to 49°C. In higher temperatures, your A/C will consume more battery power to maintain internal temperature.

Filters: the default filter is the <link=GasCarbonDioxide><color=#44AD83>Oxid uhličitý</color></link> filter, which captures the gas generated by humans when breathing out. If you are not using 100% <link=GasOxygen><color=#44AD83>Kyslík</color></link> in your breathing gas, add additional filters, eg if you mix 25% <link=GasOxygen><color=#44AD83>Kyslík</color></link> + 75% <link=GasNitrogen><color=#44AD83>Dusík</color></link>, the nitrogen will accumulate in your suit over time and suffocate you, unless you have a nitrogen filter. If you have the correct filters and breathable gas, but are still experiencing problems, use the 'Flush' function on your Space Helmet. Low/critical oxygen warnings will sound as your filters cease to function.

If damaged, your suit can be patched by holding duct tape in your hand and using 'activate' button.

ExMin.Description:
In the aftermath of the Sisyphus disaster on Mars in 2079, asteroid shifting was officially banned by the <link=ODA><color=#0080FFFF>ODA</color></link>. This sea-change forced the newborn space mining industry to reconsider its strategies, but until the opening of the Manaus Space Elevator, marginal economics meant offworld resource extraction was effectively impossible.
Formed in 2095 by a long-standing Swiss-German mining conglomerate and a consortium of other interests, ExMin was more an idea than a commercial reality for several decades. Created with the certainty that a space elevator would eventually arrive, ExMin was one of the first to exploit the access it offered. Subsequently it has become one of the Solar System's most powerful commercial entities.
With access to space secure, ExMin became a central player in the flow of resources to the Inner System. It has competition, principally from Brazilian mining giant <link=Recurso><color=#0080FFFF>Recurso</color></link>, but the company has never entirely lost its lead on off-world mining. Synonymous with rare earth metals and pioneering off-world resource extraction, it stands at the forefront of development throughout the Solar System.
ExMin.Title: ExMin

FarmingPage.Description: To survive on alien worlds, the ODA expects all Stationeers to set up viable hydroponic systems, or contact registered local resource traders. SETTING UP When setting up your hydroponic system, you will need seeds. Alternatively, you can plant the food itself. Common Stationeer hydroponic equipment includes: - Přenosná hydroponie - Hydroponická nádoba (sada) - Hydroponická stanice (sada) - Harvie All hydroponics systems require water, sunlight and the correct gas mixture - plants require Oxid uhličitý and produce oxygen (except for Mimozemská houba). PLants will not grow in the wrong atmosphere. If plants do not have enough light, you will need to build a Růstové světlo. Your system will depend on available resources and time, but a well-designed farming system can be almost fully automated given sufficient time and resources. HARVESTING Most plants have several growth stages. The first stages are the plant growing through its lifecycle. During the second-to-last phase, the plant will yield fruit but no seeds. In the final phase, seeds and fruit may be harvested from the plant. After that, unless cleared, the plant will die. FERTILIZER Fertilizer alters plant growth processes, and is created by the Portable Composter and the Advanced Composter using organic matter. Fertilizer's affects depend on its ingredients: - Food increases individual PLANT YIELD by up to 3 items - Decayed Food increases plant GROWTH SPEED up to 3 times - Biomasa increases the NUMBER OF GROWTH CYCLES the fertilizer lasts for to a maximum of 5 The effect of these ingredients depends on their respective proportions in the composter when processing is activated. Fertilizer is produced at a 1:3 ratio of fertilizer to ingredients. When processing, Dusík and Těkavé látky is released, as well a small amount of heat.
FarmingPage.Title: Growing Food

GasHydrazine.Description: <link=GasHydrazine><color=#44AD83>Hydrazine</color></link> is the perfect fuel for space exploration as it requires no oxidiser to combust, only needing heat or a spark. It is more commonly stored in it's liquid form <link=GasLiquidHydrazine><color=#44AD83>Liquid Hydrazine</color></link> which is stable at room temperature. It is extremely toxic to all forms of life.
GasHydrazine.Title: Hydrazine

GasLiquidAlcohol.Description: <link=GasLiquidAlcohol><color=#44AD83>Liquid Alcohol</color></link> is a relatively safe and versatile volatile liquid at room temperatures. When exposed to a vacuum it will decompose into <link=GasMethane><color=#44AD83>Methane</color></link> to form a small head pressure.
GasLiquidAlcohol.Title: Liquid Alcohol

GasLiquidCarbonDioxide.Description: <link=GasCarbonDioxide><color=#44AD83>Carbon Dioxide</color></link> in its liquid form. It can be created by lowering the temperature of <link=GasCarbonDioxide><color=#44AD83>Carbon Dioxide</color></link> gas below it's boiling point. GasLiquidCarbonDioxide.Title: Liquid Carbon Dioxide

This can be achieved using a <link=ThingStructureHeatExchangerGastoGas><color=green>Heat Exchanger (Gas to Gas)</color></link> or a <link=ThingStructureAirConditioner><color=green>Air Conditioner</color></link>.

GasLiquidPollutant.Description: <link=GasPollutant><color=#44AD83>Pollutant</color></link> in its liquid form. It can be created by lowering the temperature of <link=GasPollutant><color=#44AD83>Pollutant</color></link> gas below it's boiling point. This can be achieved using a <link=ThingStructureHeatExchangerGastoGas><color=green>Heat Exchanger (Gas to Gas)</color></link> or a <link=ThingStructureAirConditioner><color=green>Air Conditioner</color></link>. <link=GasLiquidPollutant><color=#44AD83>Liquid Pollutant</color></link> introduced into the atmosphere will quickly evaporate back into <link=GasPollutant><color=#44AD83>Pollutant</color></link>.

GasLiquidSilanol.Description: <link=GasSilanol><color=#44AD83>Silanol</color></link> in its liquid form is the premium refrigerant gas for utilising phase change to pump heat. With its extremely high heat capacity it also makes an excellent coolant, able to absorb large quantities of heat energy with minimal temperature fluctuation.

When exposed to a vacuum it will decompose into <link=GasPollutant><color=#44AD83>Pollutant</color></link> to form a small head pressure. At room temperature it exists as solid <link=ThingItemPureIceLiquidSodiumChloride><color=green>Salt</color></link>.

GasOzone.Description: <link=GasOzone><color=#44AD83>Ozone</color></link> is a highly energetic oxidiser. As with <link=GasNitrousOxide><color=#44AD83>Nitrous Oxide</color></link>, when mixed with a volatile gas <link=GasOzone><color=#44AD83>Ozone</color></link> will create extra hot combustion.

GeFabrik.Description:
Officially known as Gewehrfabrik GmbH, GeFabrik is one of the world’s oldest and most highly regarded armament firms, known for producing exceptionally accurate, high-end firearms.
In the wake of the European arms manufacturing collapse in the 2030s, a group of unemployed armament staff formed GeFabrik. Dedicated to renewing original design principles, the company is legendary for extensive testing, sometimes lasting as long as 10 years, in order to produce ‘ganz’ weapon formats.
GeFabrik is widely regarded as having single-handedly salvaged Germany's manufacturing reputation, while doing nothing for their sense of humor.

GeneticsPage.Description:
Plants have a set of Genes that modifies their behavior. A plant's genes will be manipulated in a number of ways, both naturally as well as artificially. When a plant produces fruit or seeds it will pass on its genetics with a small random mutation.

On top of random mutations, a plant's condition over its life can also affect its genes - for example if a plant is starved of water, while it may affect the plants growth speed and yield, the offspring will receive genes that make it require less water. In this way you can manipulate your crop's ideal conditions.

There are a number of tools you will need to manage your crops effectively: <link=ThingItemPlantSampler><color=green>Plant Sampler</color></link> and <link=ThingAppliancePlantGeneticAnalyzer><color=green>Plant Genetic Analyzer</color></link>. These tools allow you to sample a growing plant and see the state of its genes.

Plant genetics is not an exact science and will require trial and error and repeated attempts before you are able to reach your targets.

Hiiragi.Description:
Founded by Noboru Hiiragi in the aftermath of the 2110s economic bubble, Hiiragi Communications absorbed several prominent offworld assets, quickly becoming the most widely used trans-Solar System communications network.
If you’ve communicated with friends and family offworld recently, it’s been through the Hiiragi network, even if it’s been branded under one of its many child companies. Hiiragi is also the number one seller for PCD’s (Personal Communication Devices) as well as a deep, if difficult to assess investor in terrestrial telecommunication networks.

HydrationPage.Description:
Your average Stationeer needs to drink water regularly. However, arcane and possibly misguided <link=ODA><color=#0080FFFF>ODA</color></link> health and safety regulations have long denied Stationeers the right to in-suit hydration mechanisms. Instead, they must take regular drink breaks to open their helmet, and imbibe water. Doing so in an unpressurized environment is unadvised.

How often to drink? This is determined by your difficulty level, the heat of the planet and how much you like to move your body.

Water comes in many forms. At least one <link=ThingItemWaterBottle><color=green>Láhev na vodu</color></link> is supplied to Stationeers as part of their rations when landing on new planets, with more in your lander crates. These can be refilled using a <link=ThingItemWaterBottleFiller><color=green>Plnička lahví na vodu</color></link>, which must itself be connected to a liquid pipe network. The network itself can be filled using a <link=ThingStructureIceCrusher><color=green>Drtič ledu</color></link> with a suitable supply of ice.

Your thirst rate can be adjusted set on the main settings menu by adjusting your Hunger/Hydration rate slider.

MusicPage.Description: The ODA does not approve of soundtracks or other distractions. As such, Stationeers have had to create their own musical accompaniment to the demanding labor of building and maintaining off-world infrastructure. Central to this pasttime is the step sequencer, which allows Stationeers to sequence short musical patterns or loops. DIY MUSIC - GETTING STARTED 1: Connect 8 Device Step Units to your step sequencer via the data port on the lefthand side. 2: Label each step unit, then assign step units 1 through 8 on the step sequencer using the screwdiver. 3: Select the output speaker (eg Passive Speaker) where the sequencer will play the sounds. This needs to be connected to the logic network on the righthand side of the sequencer. 4: Place a Stop Watch and use a Čtečka logiky and Zapisovač logiky to write the time to the time variable on the sequencer. 5: Set the BPM on the sequencer using a Číselník and a Zapisovač logiky to write to the sequencer's BPM variable. A higher bpm will play the sequence faster. 6: Insert a sound cartridge of your chosing and select which variant of sound you wish to play by pushing the arrow buttons located above and below the sound cartidge slot. 7: Choose the pitch of the sounds to play by setting the dial on each of your 8 step units to the desired note. With drums, each note is a different drum sounds. You can trial your sounds by pushing the activate button on each step unit (with the sequencer inactive). 8: Get freaky with the Low frequency oscillator. 9: Finally, activate the sequencer, Vibeoneer.
MusicPage.Text:
The {LINK:ODA;ODA} does not approve of soundtracks or other distractions.
As such, {LINK:Stationeers;Stationeers} have had to create their own musical accompaniment to the demanding labor of building and maintaining off-world infrastructure.
Central to this pasttime is the step sequencer, which allows Stationeers to sequence short musical patterns or loops. 

{HEADER:DIY MUSIC - GETTING STARTED}

1: Connect 8 {THING:DeviceStepUnit}s to your step sequencer via the data port on the lefthand side.

2: Label each step unit, then assign step units 1 through 8 on the step sequencer using the screwdiver.

3: Select the output speaker (eg {THING:PassiveSpeaker}) where the sequencer will play the sounds. This needs to be connected to the logic network on the righthand side of the sequencer.

4: Place a {THING:StopWatch} and use a {THING:StructureLogicReader} and {THING:StructureLogicWriter} to write the time to the time variable on the sequencer.

5: Set the BPM on the sequencer using a {THING:StructureLogicDial} and a {THING:StructureLogicWriter} to write to the sequencer's BPM variable. A higher bpm will play the sequence faster. 

6: Insert a sound cartridge of your chosing and select which variant of sound you wish to play by pushing the arrow buttons located above and below the sound cartidge slot.

7: Choose the pitch of the sounds to play by setting the dial on each of your 8 step units to the desired note. With drums, each note is a different drum sounds. You can trial your sounds by pushing the activate button on each step unit (with the sequencer inactive).

8: Get freaky with the {THING:DeviceLfoVolume}.

9: Finally, activate the sequencer, Vibeoneer.
MusicPage.Title: Making Music

Norsec.Description:
With its roots in early 20th Century defense industry, Norsec (a.k.a. Northern Security Systems) was an early adopter of asteroid mining – one of its tugs being involved in the infamous Sisyphus Hit on the fledgling Martian colony at Sanders.
Norsec was officially cleared of any wrong-doing, but when the <link=ODA><color=#0080FFFF>ODA</color></link> banned asteroidal relocation, the company shifted its focus to infrastructure and manufacturing.
Norsec’s orbitally-based Space Systems Division is responsible for the design and production of <link=ODA><color=#0080FFFF>ODA</color></link>’s core transport systems, while also being rumoured to hold a large interest in <link=ExMin><color=#0080FFFF>ExMin</color></link>. The company is also noted for its willingness to engage in experimental robotic technology.
Norsec.Title: Norsec

NutritionPage.Description: HUNGER Stationeers get hungry eventually, but not all food is created equal. Also, your hunger rate varies depending on settings and difficulty. Eating will only consume that part of an item adequate to restoring your hunger to 100%. Stationeers receive supplies of food such as Agrizero Cereální tyčinka in their lander upon arriving on a new world. When these are exhausted, you must find new sources of sustenance - such as growing your own, from the seeds supplied, or contacting a Trader. NUTRITION Eating raw ingredients will satisfy hunger less than meals, ie will replace a smaller proportion of your hunger. The basic elements of food are created using hydroponics systems. These can be processed into recipe ingredients using the Zpracovatel činidel, then turned into meals using a Mikrovlnná trouba or Automated Oven. Your hunger rate can be adjusted set in the main settings menu by adjusting the Hunger/Hydration rate slider in the settings. Note that the hunger slider also governs your Thirst.
NutritionPage.Title: Hunger and nutrition

ODA.Description:
In the aftermath of the Earth Crisis, humanity’s focus on space diminished. Yet many felt that, without ambitions beyond our home planet, our species might falter.
Created in 2070CE by a newly revamped United Nations, the Offworld Development Agency was given a very specific goal - to guide and encourage human space exploration at a time the cosmos was fading from the public mind. 
It inaugurated the <link=Stationeers><color=#0080FFFF>Stationeer</color></link> Program in 2095. Understanding that funding would be difficult to come by, the ODA conceived the program as a slow-burn, low-outlay space initiative. While some derided Stationeers as 'cut-price cosmic castaways', the success of the program is testament to the wisdom and pragmatism of ODA's vision.
ODA.Title: ODA

Recurso.Description:
This long-standing Brazilian mining group branched into space in the late 21st century.
Focused primarily on bulk minerals and metals, the company is perhaps best understood as an extension of the Brazilian government – very few upper echelon political figures in modern Brazil are not implicated in one arm or another of this industrial behemoth.
Enmeshment with South American politics has given the company heavy influence over the Manaus space elevator. This deep state control has led to other groups – the <link=ODA><color=#0080FFFF>ODA</color></link> included – to exercise a certain ‘flexibility’ toward Recurso.
Accusations of illegal asteroid relocation, safety violations and numerous commercial infringements have barely touched it. Meanwhile, defenders point out that very little has been proven in court, and Recurso is hardly alone – hence the truism: 'In space, we all live in glass houses.'

Sinotai.Description:
The sole 'traditional' state entity to survive offworld politics, Sinotai’s reach and power is second only to the <link=ODA><color=#0080FFFF>ODA</color></link> itself. In many ways a relic – a sub-agency of a staggeringly complicated Earth-bound corporate-bureaucracy – its structure has allowed Sinotai to achieve incredible things.
Proving its mettle in the early 21st Century by putting the first humans on Mars, establishing the first offworld gigawatt power system, and the first space-borne fuel refinery, few space-going organisations lack some degree of relationship with Sinotai. A common joke has it that it's impossible to do anything in space without them.
Regardless of the truth, Sinotai's approach to off-world development has involved a 'soft power' approach, from MOU's with <link=Recurso><color=#0080FFFF>Recurso</color></link> (giving them preferential access to the Manaus space elevator) to murkier alliances of convenience with a range of Trader groups.

Stationeers.Description:
In the early 22nd century, Earth was emerging from a cataclysm. Its resources eroded, our population reduced, rebuilding was the spirit of the era.
Initiated by the <link=ODA><color=#0080FFFF>Offworld Development Agency</color></link> (ODA) in 2095CE, the Stationeers Program was dedicated to a single ideal: keeping humanity pointed at the stars.
Stationeers are everything: astronauts, engineers and explorers, deployed with limited equipment and tools, trained to do more with less. Turning the environment to their advantage, their job is to provide infrastructure for humans in space, at a fraction of the cost of traditional space programs.
Able to build and maintain bases anywhere from the Moon to Mimas and beyond, Stationeers are our vanguard in the cosmos. Schooled in offworld survival, mining and construction techniques, basic metallurgy, electronics, rocketry, hydroponics and more ‘arcane’ sciences, Stationeers do what they must to survive, and thrive.
Renowned for having no entry criteria, there is no such thing as a ‘typical’ Stationeer. Psychological profiling suggests successful Cadets show a ‘baseline’ pragmatism and single-mindedness, but some of the most famous Stationeers possess neither of these qualities.
Recruiting from civil engineering backgrounds, military and aerospace industries, software development, mining groups, as well as scientific fields and even religious orders, the Stationeers Program is – fundamentally – open to all humanity.
Stationeers.Title: Stationeers

TK.Description:
Originally a defense contractor specializing in brute force, high power weaponry, Tanzanian Kinetic Systems executed a large-scale, peace-time pivot to become the African Assembly’s leading designer of high-speed goods conveyors.
Now producing a range of chute network designs and components, TK has a strong offworld presence as a result of the Afro-Sino partnerships in the latter 21st Century. Based in the ‘reconned’ Kigamboni district of Dar E Salaam, the Company regularly enters into development partnerships with <link=CHAC><color=#0080FFFF></color></link> and, as a result, many of their products show distinct similarities.
        After all, what is a gun but a ‘high speed goods conveyor’.
TK.Title: TK Systems

TemperatureControlPage.Description: In order to control the temperature of a system, we have to either add heat to it thus increasing its temperature or remove heat from it thus cooling it down, that's the basic idea of temperature control. Devices that achieve this goal for you are Nástěnné topení (sada), Nástěnný chladič (sada), Potrubní radiátor, and Klimatizace. NOTE: There are many methods of temperature control. Some involve none of the devices mentioned. Here, we are covering the basics. It is important to understand your environment before you install any type of temperature control. The gas or liquid volume is an important factor to when choosing your method of temperature control. A Malá nádrž can hold up to 6000L, while a Velká nádrž can hold up to 50,000L, which means that if both are full, the small tank will react faster to temperature changes. A room is a space that can hold a certain amount of gas. The bigger it is the more volume it will be able to hold, so the same rules generally apply to tanks and rooms. PIPE NETWORKS A pipe network is one or more pipe segments connected to each other with no separation at any point. A pipe network shares the same atmosphere everywhere along the pipe, no matter how large it is. If you change the temperature or pressure at one end of the network, the furthest end will experience the same change immediately with no delay. Adding devices to a network may split it into two different networks. TradingPage.Description:
Trading is an essential part of a <link=Stationeers><color=#0080FFFF>Stationeers</color></link> existence, especially on more extreme worlds, where new cadets may be challenged at first to survive without assistance.

There are three separate tiers of contacts. These contacts have increasing difficulties to contact, and hang around for about 20 minutes before they leave and another one takes their place, so you’ll have to find the harder contacts if you want to check out many traders.

Contacts must be resolved by the dish before it can determine how accurately it is pointed at the contact.  The time to resolve is determined by the dish's power output multiplied by the dish alignment,  over the contact’s expected resolve wattage. If the contact is resolving too slowly, it likely indicates you are not close to the target at all, and you should try a very different angle. Alternately, the contact might have a very high expected wattage, and your current dish just isnt big enough to resolve it in a reasonable time. The resolving process only uses 10% of the actual power your dish is set to.

Once you have resolved the contacts position, you’ll be able to press the interrogate button.  Similar to resolving, you’ll need to land enough wattage on the contact. The interrogation dialog will inform you of the current calculations. Interrogation does have a hard minimum, and if the dish is not pointed well enough, or the power is too low, you won't be able to start the process. Interrogation also has a time requirement, with harder contacts taking significantly longer, so you’ll want to use high wattages to ensure you finish before the trader moves on.  Once interrogation is complete, you can land the trader just as before.

WeatherPage.Description:
The Solar System's planets are not as calm as they may seem. After seven days on any world with an atmosphere, the inscrutable forces of nature swing into action – hitting unwary Stationeers with blizzards, dust storms and volcanic events.

As such, the <link=ODA><color=#0080FFFF>ODA</color></link> recommends that freshly deployed Stationeers create an airtight base within 7 days of landing.

Any dynamic objects left outside in a storm – on Mars, Loulan, Vulcan or Europa – risks being blown far, far away, including your lander.

Likewise, be aware that solar panels are fragile and may have their glass shattered, or occasionally even be destroyed by a sufficiently ferocious storm. During storms, their output is also drastically reduced.

Xigo.Description:
A 2150CE survey revealed the Xigo 'X' as one of the most recognized symbols in the world. Yet few participants could clearly describe the company's actual scope.
Precisely where the company begins and ends has been the subject of endless theories, financial studies and lawsuits – originally a website for price comparisons, the conglomerate expanded to embrace data, then distribution and finally production.
It was a seemingly indiscriminate expansion, focused not on one industry, but all of them – taking in so many fields that business analysts have largely rejected the idea of Xigo as a single entity. Rather, it is a conceptual grouping for a branch of human activity. And while such statistics are – by their very nature – difficult to confirm, recent estimates suggest Xigo employs over 1.5% of the entire human race.
Suffice to say, it produces almost everything.
